title: fix(react): the objectui#9571 `data` strip now reaches the legacy `props` alias bag (objectui#9758)
body:
Fixes #9758

Ruling: decision batch #167 item 2, letter 剥, maintainer 「其他同意」 2026-09-18T15:17Z (comment `5732098890`). Quoted verbatim, not paraphrased:

> the objectui#9571 strip is applied to the legacy `props` alias bag as well — the same arm predicate `recordSourceDataArmForType(type) === 'view-data'`, the same dev diagnostic — so an authored `props: { data }` loses the prop seat exactly as top-level `data` and `properties: { data }` already do; ⛔ no validator refusal, ⛔ no change to what the alias otherwise carries

## The corpus, measured at source

Base `origin/main` `d6a84446f`, read 2026-09-18T20:10Z; branched from that commit.

The props object `SchemaRenderer` builds for `createElement` has **seven** spread sites, in this order:

1. `...outgoingComponentProps` — the node's own non-metadata keys, which objectui#9571 already strips
2. `...outgoingPropsBag` — the legacy `props` alias bag, narrowed by `propsWithoutCanonicalKeys` (objectui#5123)
3. `...ariaProps`
4. `...debugAttrs`
5. the conditional `data-testid` (objectui#8268)
6. the conditional `data-obj-schema-invalid`
7. `...props` — this component's own React props, spread LAST, which is the HOST carrier objectui#9571 deliberately refused to gate

Site 2 runs after site 1, so the strip at site 1 was undone one line later for anyone who spelled the key `props: { data }`. The canonical `properties: { data }` does not escape, because the evaluation memo's hoist copies `properties.*` onto the node before the metadata destructure — the value is in `componentProps` and site 1 sees it. The alias bag is never hoisted, which is exactly why it survived.

## Premise reading, pre-fix — three spellings, one instrument

Run 2026-09-18T20:15:31Z on the base commit, `packages/react/src/__tests__/SchemaRenderer.legacyPropsDataStrip-9758.test.tsx`, over all nine object-arm registry keys. The assertion is one labelled object so the failure NAMES the arm:

```
  {
    "canonical `properties: { data }`": false,
-   "legacy `props: { data }`": false,
+   "legacy `props: { data }`": true,
    "top-level `data`": false,
  }
```

The two same-subject controls fire in the same command and return `false`; only the legacy spelling returns `true`. That is what makes the third row a reading rather than a broken probe. Pre-fix tally: 15 failed, 12 passed of 27.

## The change

`packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx`, 20 lines of code plus comments:

- one helper, `withoutAuthoredDataKey(bag, refuse)`, which both outgoing bags now go through. Identity is the signal: the `in` test comes first, a bag declaring no `data` is handed back ITSELF with no copy allocated, and each call site reads `result !== bag` to decide whether to warn — so the decision is never computed twice and cannot disagree with what was actually spread.
- the arm is read ONCE, into `refusesAuthoredDataProp`, and handed to both call sites. Two independent lookups of the same question is the shape that let the alias keep the seat in the first place.
- ⛔ The HOST path is untouched. `...props` is still spread last and still wins; Option B was refused on objectui#9571 and stays refused.
- ⛔ No validator change, no allowlist of block NAMES, and nothing else the alias carries moves.

## The one judgement call in the diff, stated rather than buried

The strip now runs **before** the objectui#6708 dropped-bag notice reads the outgoing bag, so that notice stops naming `data` on this arm. Both of its sentences become false for that key after this change: it says the key "is spread as React props on the created element" (it is not, any more) and it tells the author to "write them under `properties` instead" (which loses the seat as well). The author still gets exactly one accurate line — the objectui#9571 warning, which now fires for the alias carrier too. Every OTHER key the alias drops is still named on the same node.

The mirror-image decision next door is deliberate and is now written down in both places: the objectui#4795 unevaluated-expression scan keeps reading the WIDER bag, because an unevaluated placeholder inside an authored `data` is still in front of a user after the strip. Its subject survives; the objectui#6708 notice's subject does not.

## Ablation — the fix proved by removing it

Run 2026-09-18T20:34Z from the committed state, driver `trap`-guarded on EXIT/INT/TERM with absolute paths.

| leg | reading |
|---|---|
| HEAD blob of `SchemaRenderer.tsx` | `d5a4d772777b13d20e047de024a1b9a5b4603196` |
| worktree hash before mutation | `d5a4d772777b13d20e047de024a1b9a5b4603196` — equal, so the mutation starts from HEAD |
| anchor / mutant occurrences BEFORE | 1 / 0 |
| mutated file hash | `f457b5ba319fa675bc0a3405666ee07d8653877b` — moved, so the write reached disk |
| anchor / mutant occurrences AFTER | 0 / 1, and the mutated line read back off disk |
| mutated run | exit 1 — **15 failed, 12 passed**, and the three-arm diff is byte-identical to the pre-fix reading above: only `legacy props: { data }` flips to `true`, both controls stay `false` |
| restored file hash | `d5a4d772777b13d20e047de024a1b9a5b4603196` — equals the HEAD blob |
| `git diff HEAD` / `git status --porcelain` after restore | both empty |
| restored run | exit 0 — 27 passed of 27 |

The mutation was a single token: the new call site's arm argument forced to `false`, which disables the alias half and leaves objectui#9571's half intact. It is the input the two implementations disagree about — an authored `props: { data: [...] }` on an object-arm block — and nothing else moves.

No build is involved in either leg: the root vitest config aliases every `@object-ui/*` specifier to that package's `src`, so the run reads the mutated source directly. That is stated because a green ablation leg that silently read a stale `dist` would be the failure this discipline exists to catch.

## Verification

Every run below went through the shared seat lock (`OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT=1`); the verdict quoted is the line the lock itself prints, not a bare shell status.

| what | verdict |
|---|---|
| `vitest run packages/react/ packages/plugin-grid/ packages/plugin-map/ packages/plugin-gantt/ packages/plugin-list/` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` — **405 test files, 4130 tests passed**, 2026-09-18T20:19Z |
| the new pin plus the objectui#9571 and objectui#6708 pins it sits beside | `VERDICT command-exit 0` — 3 files, 102 tests passed |
| `turbo run type-check lint --filter @object-ui/react` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` — 0 errors (363 pre-existing warnings) |
| `check:control-bytes` | exit 0 — 8016 tracked text files scanned |
| `check:new-line-citations` | exit 0 — 0 new cross-file line citations |
| `check:test-path-roots` | exit 0 |
| `check:changeset-claims` | exit 0, report-only |
| `check:pending-changeset-literals` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — 1 released package's source changed, 1 changeset declared |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on all three paths | NOT GOVERNED — 3 paths checked against 5 governed surfaces, none matched |

One lint warning lands on the new test file (`Modifying a variable defined outside a component or hook`) at the props-capture line. Control: the pre-existing objectui#9571 pin produces the byte-identical warning at the byte-identical construct, and its own doc comment records that this is the spelling the rule permits for a render-time capture. Not a new class, and a warning, not an error.

The repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` are CI's runs and were not taken here.

## What was NOT measured

- **Not measured end-to-end.** Like its objectui#9571 predecessor, this pin reads the props bag `SchemaRenderer` hands over — the only lens that can tell the two carriers apart. Whether a real grid then draws is the plugin packages' half, and their suites are in the green sweep above but none of them authors `props: { data }` today.
- **Not measured: any authored corpus outside this repo.** A repo-wide grep finds no authored `props: { data }` in `packages/`, `apps/`, `examples/` or `content/`; the only hits are test fixtures on types that are NOT on the object arm, plus one `plugin-grid` test whose `props` is the React-prop argument of its own helper, not `schema.props`. Downstream metadata is out of reach from here.
- **Not re-derived:** the arm table's rows. They belong to `recordSourceDataArmForType` and are kept honest by the registry-derived pins in `plugin-grid` and `plugin-map`; the new pin re-reads them through the predicate so this file cannot drift from the table.

## Docs

No doc or README in this repo carries objectui#9571, and none shows a `props: { data }` spelling, so nothing here states something this change makes false. Checked rather than assumed.

## Landing

Draft, and it stays draft — landing is the seat's act. No ready flip, no auto-merge, no merge.
